summary: Light steel tower in Torch River No. 488, Saskatchewan; new cupola 1957, towermen listed to 2002, and the 2020 English Fire was named for a tower near it. Current status not found.

events.note: Major repairs to keep the tower in service, per the Department of Natural Resources annual report for 1952-53.
Tower completely overhauled, per the Department of Natural Resources annual report for 1963-64.
John Charles is listed at English Cabin from 1986 to 1993.
Allan Klamot is listed at English Cabin from 1995 to 2002.
Latest year in the towermen list for English Cabin.
The English Fire began on May 8, 2020, and was named for a fire tower near English Cabin where it was first reported.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.ca places the tower on Lars Road in Torch River No. 488, while the Department of Natural Resources reports place it in the Fort a la Corne Forest Reserve. The story gives both names; the sources do not contradict each other directly.

Only one water bomber used to fight English Fire: Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency

notes_for_editor: No source gives the build date. The 1915-16 Fort a la Corne report names two 80-foot steel towers but not English Cabin, so it is not tied to this tower. Height 80 ft comes from the websiteservice tower list; Firelookout.ca lists no height. Global News (2020) is the only source on current use, calling the site a tourist site. No current status, access or visit source was found. The Facebook post on the English Cabin tower and an SPSA detection-tower list were not checked.
